entry.title: Take-aways from NVIDIA GTC 2026!
entry.content:
I recently attended NVIDIA GTC 2026 in San Jose, California - one of the premier AI and deep learning conferences. Here are my key takeaways:

NVIDIA GTC 2026 - San Jose Convention Center

TL;DR: NVIDIA is evolving from a chip company to a full-stack systems provider, betting big on agentic AI and inference workloads. Security concerns and strategic partnerships are shaping the next phase of AI deployment.

Key Takeaways

1. Evolution from “Chip Company” to “Systems Company”

The overarching theme was NVIDIA’s shift away from being identified solely by GPUs: NVIDIA is now selling full racks (Vera Rack), entire data center “pods,” and integrated networking solutions.

  • Scale: NVIDIA is positioning itself to handle a “trillion dollars” in business by 2027 by providing the entire computing stack, including CPUs, LPUs (via their Groq acquisition), and networking.
  • Heterogeneous Computing: Moving toward a hybrid model that includes ARM-based and Intel/AMD integrations to meet diverse compute requirements beyond just AI training.

2. The Rise of Agentic AI and “OpenClaw”

A major focus was the transition toward autonomous agents that can act on behalf of users.

  • OpenClaw & NemoClaw: NVIDIA is leaning into OpenClaw (an open-source agentic framework) and introduced NemoClaw, which they describe as an “enterprise-grade,” hardened version.
  • The “ChatGPT Moment”: CEO Jensen Huang characterized this move toward agentic AI as a pivotal industry shift, moving from simple chat interfaces to autonomous personal and enterprise assistants.

3. Pivot from Training to Inference

The AI marketplace is rapidly moving away from massive model training toward inference (running the models in real-world applications).

  • Workload Shift: Forecasts suggest 80–85% of AI workloads will soon be inference-based.
  • Edge Distribution: Inference requires lower power and cost than training. NVIDIA is now pushing “cost per token” efficiency in their monster systems to remain competitive against power-constrained edge devices.

4. Strategic Partnerships: Cisco and the “AI Grid”

NVIDIA is increasingly relying on partners to penetrate markets where they lack their own service and maintenance infrastructure.

  • The AI Grid: A collaboration with Cisco to use existing network infrastructure and RTX Pro Blackwell GPUs to create a “web of inferencing” at the network edge.
  • Latency vs. Speed: For physical AI (like robotics), the focus has shifted from bandwidth to latency, requiring the 20–30ms response times that specialized networking partners provide.

5. Security and “Physical AI” Risks

As AI moves from digital screens to the physical world (robotics, industrial tools), the stakes for security have evolved.

  • Hardening Agents: There are significant concerns regarding how “hardened” these agentic frameworks truly are against threat actors.
  • Safe Deployment: Did the rapid timeline from the release of OpenClaw to “enterprise-grade” NemoClaw allow for sufficient security testing? Security must be wrapped around the entire “AI Factory.”

Key Tech Terminology: GTC 2026

Term Description
LPU Language Processing Unit (acquired via Groq) designed for fast, low-cost inference.
NemoClaw NVIDIA’s branded, secure implementation of the OpenClaw agent framework.
AI-RAN AI-Radio Access Network; integrating AI into telco infrastructure (e.g., T-Mobile/Nokia).
Vera Rack A full CPU rack designed to support diverse, agentic AI requirements.
entry.summary: Key insights and takeaways from NVIDIA GTC 2026 in San Jose, California

entry.title: Wrapping up AWS re:Invent 2021!
entry.content:
Wrapping up a very exciting week at AWS re:Invent 2021 in Las Vegas. Very humbled and grateful for spending a few days learning from and networking with some of the top professionals in cloud technology. Here is my personal recap.

AWS re:Invent 2021 — Las Vegas

TL;DR: AWS re:Invent 2021 featured one of the most significant announcements for financial markets infrastructure in recent years: Nasdaq and AWS unveiled a multi-year partnership to bring market infrastructure to the cloud. On the machine learning front, AWS introduced tighter Amazon EMR integration in SageMaker Studio, launched the free SageMaker Studio Lab, and announced a new scholarship program to help broaden access to AI and ML education.

Nasdaq and AWS: Bringing Capital Markets to the Cloud

One of the biggest moments of the conference came when Nasdaq CEO Adena Friedman joined AWS CEO Adam Selipsky on stage to announce a multi-year strategic partnership between Nasdaq and AWS.

The collaboration marks a significant step toward modernizing capital markets infrastructure by leveraging cloud technologies. Beyond migrating market infrastructure, the partnership also explores opportunities across Nasdaq’s anti-financial crime platforms, data and analytics offerings, and market technology solutions.

For an industry where reliability, resilience, and performance are paramount, this announcement represents an important milestone in the ongoing evolution of financial markets.

SageMaker Studio Meets Amazon EMR

AWS also announced a long-awaited improvement for data scientists working with large-scale data processing.

Amazon SageMaker Studio now provides native integration with Amazon EMR, allowing users to create, discover, manage, and connect to EMR clusters directly from the Studio interface—even across shared AWS accounts within an organization.

The integration also includes built-in access to Spark UI, making it easier to monitor, troubleshoot, and debug distributed Spark workloads. Together, these improvements significantly streamline the experience of building machine learning pipelines that rely on large-scale data processing.

SageMaker Studio Lab: Free Machine Learning for Everyone

In another announcement focused on accessibility, AWS introduced the public preview of Amazon SageMaker Studio Lab.

The free service allows anyone to learn and experiment with machine learning without needing an AWS account, a credit card, or prior cloud infrastructure experience. By lowering the barrier to entry, Studio Lab provides an accessible environment for students, hobbyists, and aspiring practitioners to gain hands-on experience with ML.

Since access is initially limited, interested users should consider requesting an account early.

Building a More Inclusive AI Community

One announcement that resonated beyond the technology itself was AWS’s new scholarship program aimed at helping underrepresented and underserved students prepare for careers in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

According to the Pew Research Center, Hispanic workers make up only 8% of the STEM workforce in the United States. Increasing representation in AI and technology requires expanding access to education and opportunities, and initiatives like this scholarship program are a meaningful step in that direction.

The program is expected to support more than 2,000 students each year, helping create a broader and more diverse pipeline of future AI and ML professionals.
entry.summary: My recap of AWS re:Invent 2021 in Las Vegas — Nasdaq's cloud partnership announcement and the week's ML/AI highlights
